subject: MaplePay quick follow-up: hosted evaluation preflight & deployment preference
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lang <tom.lang@maplepay.com>, Priya Singh <priya@maplepay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: MaplePay quick follow-up: hosted evaluation preflight & deployment preference

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can scope a short hosted evaluation:

- Goal: validate low-latency inline checkout scoring (P95 < 200ms) and edge routing for EU customers.
- Ask from our side: a small pilot dataset + typical production traffic profile (CSV preferred) so we can pre-configure endpoints, batching, and KV-prefix caching.
- Deployment preference check: you mentioned wanting to keep data in your VPC long-term, but you were open to a Hosted API pilot to move faster. Would you prefer we: (A) kick off a Hosted API evaluation now and assess leakage/egress needs, or (B) scope a Dedicated pool / VPC on day 1? For the pilot we typically recommend Hosted to iterate faster unless compliance blocks it.

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (video), maplepay_prod_traffic.csv (sample you promised)

Proposed next steps:
1) You share the traffic sample (if not already attached).
2) We provision a Hosted sandbox endpoint and a short runbook for tests (48–72h).
3) If Hosted looks good, we map SLA and Dedicated/VPC requirements for an expanded proof-of-concept.

Can you confirm the pilot preference and whether we should include SSO/KMS requirements for the sandbox?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0192

Thanks Dylan — good demo. A couple of clarifying points before we hand this to infra: 

1) For the Hosted pilot, what are the default per-endpoint rate limits and burst behavior? Our checkout traffic has spiky bursts around payroll windows and we need predictable tail latency.
2) Can you confirm how Redwood handles tokenization/PII during the Hosted pilot? We will need to redact cardholder data and ensure no full PANs are stored.
3) If we start Hosted and decide to move to Dedicated/VPC, what is the migration path and expected downtime?

We can share a redacted traffic sample by EOD. Prefer Hosted pilot if the rate/burst profile can be tuned.

Tom

Subject: Re: MaplePay quick follow-up: hosted evaluation preflight & deployment preference

Tom — thanks for the quick notes. Looping Monica (CS lead) and Vivek (solutions/infra) to answer the rate-limit and data handling questions and to own the sandbox provisioning. 

Short answers: 
- Rate limits: Hosted sandbox defaults to a soft quota of 600 rps per endpoint with a burst window that allows short spikes up to ~2x (subject to fair-use and tenant isolation). We can request a tuned quota for your pilot based on the CSV traffic profile you provide.
- Tail latency: our P95 guarantees in Hosted pilots depend on endpoint configuration (batching LP vs single-token streaming). For inline scoring we typically use single-token streaming with batching disabled at the endpoint to prioritize tail latency; that path has produced P95s < 200ms in our benchmarks for similar models. We'll run a short latency sweep in the sandbox.
- PII/tokenization: Redwood hosted endpoints can be configured with on-write redaction and customer-provided tokenization hooks. We DO NOT store PANs by default; we recommend sending a hashed token for card references during the pilot. Monica will coordinate the exact masking guide.
- Migration to Dedicated/VPC: we support zero-downtime routing cutovers by running compat model variants in parallel for a brief canary window (usually < 2 hours), but dedicated provisioning lead times (GPU pool sizing + network peering) can be 2–6 business days depending on capacity.

Monica/Vivek — can you provision a Hosted sandbox for MaplePay with an initial soft quota of 1k rps (based on their burst needs) and a data-retention TTL of 24 hours for the pilot? If that's heavy, propose a recommendation and we’ll loop legal for SSO/KMS notes.

Thanks,
Dylan

Thanks Dylan/Tom — happy to take this. Quick plan and owner assignments: 

1) I will spin up a Hosted sandbox endpoint in prod-us-east with the following initial config: 2 endpoints (scoring and batch-run), soft quota 1000 rps per scoring endpoint, burst policy set to 2x sustained for 60s. Retention 24h for logs, 7d for metrics. Sandbox endpoint URL and API key will be shared in a secure doc link.
2) Vivek will prepare a short runbook (latency sweep, concurrency test, tokenization checklist) and will join your infra call if you want a live test.
3) For data controls: we will provide a masking guide (send hashed tokens for card refs) and a sample webhook that strips PANs before ingest.

Deliverables and timeline:

- +48h: run the initial latency/concurrency sweep and share results.
